DISAGREEMENT on rider level: Merchant site says "Intermediate"; evo says "Intermediate-Advanced"; King Snow and SnowboardingProfiles say advanced-to-expert. The manufacturer spec states Intermediate, but reviewers consistently recommend it for more advanced riders. [24][4][27] 32. Target rider: Aggressive freestyle riders who want a twin that can handle high speeds, big jumps, and tech tricks [27] 33. Not recommended for beginners: "Not for beginners and even most intermediate riders will find this board a bit too much" [17] 34. Sizes below 150cm made with softer/women-friendly stiffness: "the sizes below 150 are made with more women-friendly stiffness" [66] SHAPE & PROFILE 35. This is common — on-snow feel often registers stiffer than manufacturer ratings. [24][27][SnowboardingProfiles] CORE & CONSTRUCTION 49. Core material: Super Fly II 700G [6][21] 50. Core description: "Stronger and lighter woods target specific areas of the core to provide pop, strength, and reduced weight" [21] 51. Core zones: Dualzone EGD — "wood grain positioned along toe and heel edges on two continuous zones, perpendicular to the rest of the wood core for consistent edge-hold and added strength" [21] 52. Core profiling: Squeezebox — "thicker, more powerful core sections with thinner, more flexible sections" improving "pop and performance" [21] 53. Fiberglass type: Triax Fiberglass — "Versatile flex and response for everything from mini to mega shred" [21] 54. Carbon reinforcement: Carbon I-Beam — "ultra-light carbon backbone increases pop and longitudinal snap" [21] 55.
